Some electricity poles in sections of Northern Cape can have bird nests on them. These can either be large nests covering the entire pole top, or more rarely be smaller nests visible on a part of the pole top. The bigger ones are often visible quite far away.

Eastern Cape license plates can be spotted through blur with a yellow section on top of a green section left of the centre of the plate, combined with white either side of this pattern. These are most similar to North West plates, but their plates have a green blur visible along the entire bottom of the plate instead of just below the yellow part. A yellow/green on the very right of the plate can sometimes be seen too.
Traffic lights in Johannesburg have three lines of reflective tape on them. This isn't found anywhere else in the country.

Kruger National Park in the north-east of the country uses a unique Google car not found anywhere else in the world. The car looks like a standard roof-rack car but the front of the car has a camoflague pattern. Some of the coverage (mostly the main roads) has been overwritten by Gen 4 coverage though, so you can still get a round here that doesn't have this unique car.

North West license plates can be spotted through blur with a thin green line across the bottom and 1 or 2 sections of yellow on the left half of the plate. These are most similar to Free State plates, but their plates often have more green visible through blur and the yellow section is more often visible on the right of Free State plates rather than the left.

Northern Cape license plates can be spotted through blur with either a yellow section across the right-most 2/3 of the plate, or a G-Y-G-Y-G pattern due to the green letters of the plate. These are most similar to Free State plates, but Free State plates should have more green visible through the blur.

Pine tree plantations are mostly found in KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumulanga. It is possible to be driving through them, see them from a distance, or both. Neighbouring Eswatini also has a lot of these so make sure you know what country you are in. One easy way to tell is Eswatini only has Gen 3 camera coverage with a white google car, whereas South Africa will often have Gen 4 camera coverage with a blue car, or Gen 2 camera coverage.

Mountains that are predominantly rocky with very little or no vegetation are most common in Western Cape. The mountains here are often tall with steep sides rather than gradual slopes, and the mountains are often closer to the camera than mountains found elsewhere in the country.
This A-shaped pole top with all 3 insulators being vertical is almost exclusive to Western Cape. It shows up often in the state which makes it one of the most crucial pole tops to remember.
Sugarcane plantations are mostly found in KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumulanga. These are especially common around the Durban area and near Eswatini.
This diagonal or triangle pole top is most common in North West and Limpopo, but is also seen regularly in Mpumalanga and sometimes in Gauteng and Free State.
This trident pole top is almost exclusive to KwaZulu-Natal. It shows up often in the state which makes it one of the most crucial pole tops to remember.

Vineyards are found in very few places other than Western Cape. The vineyards can be seen in different seasons so it is important to recognize what they look like in both summer coverage and winter coverage. In summer, they will look like the picture below. In winter, they will lose their leaves but the vines will still be in neat rows.
This A-shaped pole top with the bottom insulators being horizontal is almost exclusive to Eastern Cape. This pole top does not show up too often but should be reliable when it does.
